card.job: Return to the one obvious previous place.
card.purpose: A link with a left arrow and a label such as "Back to dashboard". The arrow travels a few pixels on hover. Use it when there is one place to return to, not a hierarchy.
useWhen: A detail or a result screen has one parent to return to.
A phone screen needs a way back to its list.

avoidWhen.when: The screen is several levels deep.
The action cancels or dismisses a task in a dialog.
The history is a flow.

keyboard.does: Follows the link.

card.job: Show where this screen sits and jump to a parent.
card.purpose: A list of links ending in the current page. Use it when a screen is several levels deep, such as a run inside a monitor. The last item is a span with aria-current="page". Wrap it in nav with aria-label="Breadcrumb".
useWhen: A screen is three or more levels deep and people need to go up to any parent.
The hierarchy is fixed: workspace, project, item.

avoidWhen.when: There is one obvious place to return to.
The path is a flow in a set order.
Content is paged.

states.name: current
states.how: aria-current="page" on the last item

parts.role: The nav; holds an ol of li items.

keyboard.does: Moves between the links.

card.job: Start an action or confirm a choice with one press.
card.purpose: The native button in Fire's soft style: a quiet fill that darkens on hover, with one primary per view. Variants and sizes are data attributes; loading, held and disabled come from aria-busy, aria-pressed, aria-expanded and disabled. On touch devices every size grows to a 40px target.
useWhen: An action runs on this page and nothing navigates: save, create, send, copy, retry.
A dialog, sheet or confirmation needs its confirm and cancel actions.
A toolbar needs icon-only actions (add data-icon-only and an aria-label).

avoidWhen.when: The action is a link to another page, or sits inside a sentence.
avoidWhen.instead: The text button (fd-btn-text), part of this component.

avoidWhen.when: Several related actions belong together as one control.
avoidWhen.instead: The button group (fd-btn-group), part of this component.

avoidWhen.when: One floating action stays visible while the page scrolls.
The user picks one option of several, or switches a setting on and off.
Delete or revoke runs without a confirmation step.
avoidWhen.instead: Put it behind a dialog or confirm; use the danger variant on the confirming button.

states.name: loading
states.how: aria-busy="true"; keeps the width and shows a spinner

states.name: held
states.how: aria-pressed="true" or aria-expanded="true"; uses the pressed fill

states.name: disabled
states.how: disabled

states.name: copied
states.how: data-state="done" on a fd-btn-swap child, set by fire.js for 1.4s after a copy

variants.useWhen: The one action the view exists for; at most one per view.
On a filled or busy surface where the default wash would disappear.
Dismissals and toolbar actions that should stay quiet.
A single upsell or confirm on a quiet panel; never beside a primary.
An accent-tinted action that is not the primary.
The confirming button of a destructive action, inside a confirmation.
A destructive action shown before any confirmation, such as Revoke in a row.
Inside dense rows and chips.
In toolbars and table rows.
Forms and dialogs that want a larger target.
A hero or a landing page call to action.
The button holds only an icon; it needs aria-label or data-fd-tooltip.
The button fills its row, as in a phone dialog footer.

parts.role: The button; a button, a or input element.
Wraps two children that swap in place, as a copy button's label and its Copied confirmation.
Joins related buttons into one control.
An action written as text inside a sentence or a card footer.

keyboard.does: Activates the button.

card.job: Tick one or more options, or a yes that saves with the form.
card.purpose: 16px box with a 4px radius and one hairline. Checked fills with the accent and draws a tick; indeterminate draws a dash. The label is part of the control, so the whole line is the target. data-fd-checkall on a parent shows indeterminate and ticks or clears its children.
useWhen: Several options may be chosen from a fixed set.
A yes or no is saved with the rest of the form, not at once.
A select-all parent controls a group of children.

avoidWhen.when: A setting takes effect the moment it changes.
Exactly one of a few options is chosen.
Each option needs a title, a sentence or a price.
A table row is selected; use the table's own selection.

states.name: checked
states.how: checked on the input

states.name: indeterminate
states.how: input.indeterminate = true, or data-fd-checkall on a parent

states.name: invalid
states.how: aria-invalid="true" on the input

states.name: disabled
states.how: disabled

parts.role: The label that wraps the input.
The drawn box; forms.js adds the tick and dash.
The tick path inside the box.

keyboard.does: Toggles the focused checkbox.

card.job: Browse a catalogue by category.
card.purpose: A category strip, lighter than tabs: no underline, just ink. The selected chip turns weight 450 and its width is reserved up front so neighbours never shift. Link chips mark the current category with aria-current="page"; button chips are single-select with aria-pressed and fire fd:change. It scrolls sideways and fades at the clipped edge.
useWhen: A catalogue, gallery or template list is narrowed by category.
There are more categories than a segmented control holds.

avoidWhen.when: The items switch views of one object.
There are two to five exclusive options.
The filters combine and apply together.
The items are settings pages.

states.name: current
states.how: aria-current="page" on a link chip, or aria-pressed="true" on a button chip

states.name: overflowing
states.how: data-overflow="start|end|both", set by nav.js

variants.useWhen: Content is clipped at the start.
Content is clipped at the end.
Content is clipped at both ends.

parts.role: One category; a link or a button.

keyboard.does: Moves between chips.
Select a button chip; Enter follows a link chip.

card.job: Choose from options that each need a title and a sentence.
card.purpose: A selectable card over a real radio or checkbox. Selected is one accent hairline, a faint accent wash and a check. Put the whole decision in the card: a title, one sentence and at most one figure on the right. Lay out as a list for a few options or as a grid (data-layout="grid") for scannable sets.
useWhen: Plans, permission levels or modes where each option needs explaining.
Each option has a price or one key figure.
Several of a fixed set may be picked, with enough to say about each (checkbox inside).

avoidWhen.when: The options are plain labels.
The options are plain labels and several may be ticked.
The choice filters what is shown and has no explanation.
The card opens something instead of selecting.

states.name: selected
states.how: checked on the input inside

states.name: disabled
states.how: disabled on the input

variants.useWhen: Many cards that people scan side by side.

parts.role: Groups cards; carries role="radiogroup" for single choice.
The label that wraps the input.
A figure on the right, such as a price.

keyboard.does: Native: move between the radio cards of a group.
Selects or toggles the focused card.

card.job: Edit raw code or JSON that has to be valid.
card.purpose: A text area in the code face with a head showing the language and an optional Format button. Tab inserts two spaces. data-fd-json checks the value on blur and on submit and writes the parser's reason and line into the field's error. Without script it is a plain text area. It is for the few places raw code is the input, never a stand-in for a control that fits better.
useWhen: An expert overrides configuration by hand and the value is JSON.
The input is code and needs checking: a template, a schema, a config override.

avoidWhen.when: The value is a list, a map or a choice that a control fits.
The value is a map of names to values.
The text is prose.
The code is shown, not edited.

states.name: invalid JSON
states.how: aria-invalid="true" with the reason in .fd-field-error, set by data-fd-json

states.name: ready
states.how: data-ready set by the script; the Format button shows

parts.role: Row with the language and the Format button.

keyboard.does: Inserts two spaces.
Leaves the field.

card.job: Keep a narrow block readable on a wide page.
card.purpose: A bounded column with a maximum width (data-size xs, sm, md, lg or xl) that stays centred when data-align="center". Use it so text and forms stop at a readable measure while the page stays wide.
useWhen: A form, an article or an empty state sits on a wide page and should not stretch.
A page has one main column in the middle.

avoidWhen.when: A form should set its own width.
A main area has a side panel.
Content is in equal columns.

variants.useWhen: A very narrow block.
A narrow block, such as a sign-in card.
A reading width.
A wide reading column.
The widest column.
The column sits in the middle of the page.

card.job: Pick from a long list by typing to filter it.
card.purpose: A text field with a listbox that uses the Popover API, so it layers above everything and closes on outside clicks. Type to filter, arrow keys to move, Enter to choose. Options are role="option" rows with an optional icon, description and mono meta. The multiple variant keeps choices as removable tokens. Fires fd:open, fd:close, fd:select and fd:change.
useWhen: The list is long enough that people need to type to find an item.
Each option needs an icon, a description or a meta label (a model, a team member).
Several items may be chosen and shown as tokens (data-multiple).

avoidWhen.when: The list is short and plain.
People may enter values that are not on a list.
The choice runs a command or jumps to a page.
The options are two to four visible labels.

states.name: open
states.how: data-state="open" on the wrapper; the listbox is shown

states.name: multiple
states.how: data-multiple on the wrapper; choices become tokens

states.name: no match
states.how: data-empty="No matches" text shows when the filter finds nothing

parts.role: The wrapper; carries data-fd-combobox and data-name.

keyboard.does: Opens the list, then moves to the next option.
Opens the list at the last option, then moves up.
Chooses the active option, or closes the list.
Closes the list.
Closes the list and moves on.
In multiple mode with an empty field: removes the last token.

card.job: Show a value people copy, such as an address or an ID.
card.purpose: A read-only value with a copy button, in the same field shape. Copy always copies the whole data-value, and a check shows for a moment (fd:copy). data-mask="end" keeps the readable start and the last few characters with dots between; it stays masked with no reveal button, so leave the button out when nobody may see the value.
useWhen: A webhook URL, endpoint, ID or an invite link is shown for copying.
An address is recognised by its last characters (data-mask="end").

avoidWhen.when: The value is secret and may be revealed or rotated.
The value is a command or code with several lines.
The value is editable.
The copy button sits inside a field people also type in.

states.name: copied
states.how: data-state="copied" for a moment after the copy

variants.useWhen: Show the start up to data-mask-from, eight dots and the last few characters.
Keep the first and last eight characters.
Show only dots.

parts.role: The wrapper; carries data-fd-secret and data-value.
An optional label inside the field.
The part that shortens with an ellipsis.
The part that is never cut off.

keyboard.does: On the copy button: copies the value.

card.job: Stop the page until the person finishes or dismisses one task.
card.purpose: A native dialog opened with showModal(): the page behind is washed out and blurred, focus moves into it and returns to the trigger. Escape, a close button and a backdrop click close it, and fd:close fires once per close whichever way it ended. Below 640px it becomes a bottom sheet you can drag down. Multi-step flows use sections with data-step.
useWhen: The task must finish or be dismissed before the page makes sense again: create a key, choose providers.
A short form needs its own focus, with confirm and cancel at the foot.
A flow has two or three steps, such as create then show the secret once.

avoidWhen.when: A destructive action needs the person to type a name before it runs.
The content is a side panel the person may leave open while working.
The content is a short list of actions on one trigger.
The content is a summary or a small picker that closes on outside click.
The message is feedback after an action and needs no decision.

states.name: open
states.how: openDialog(id), a trigger with data-fd-dialog-open="id", or showModal()

states.name: persistent
states.how: data-static on the dialog keeps backdrop clicks from closing it

states.name: reset on open
states.how: data-reset on the dialog resets its forms each time it opens

states.name: step
states.how: section[data-step] with buttons [data-fd-dialog-step="next|prev|name"]

states.name: busy step
states.how: data-fd-dialog-step-delay="600" on the step button

variants.useWhen: A confirmation or a one-field form (400px).
A form with several fields or a short list (640px).
A picker with a toolbar and a grid (800px).

parts.role: The heading; focus lands here when the body has no field.
The scrolling content; edge shadows show when it overflows.
The actions: cancel first, the confirming button last.
The corner close button; carries data-fd-dialog-close.
Step dots in a multi-step dialog.

keyboard.does: Closes the dialog.
Moves between controls inside the dialog; focus does not leave it.

card.job: Separate two groups with a hairline.
card.purpose: A one-pixel rule in the faint line colour. data-vertical makes it a vertical rule that stretches to the height of a row. With fd-grow it fills a row on either side of a word such as "or".
useWhen: Two groups in a toolbar or a menu need a quiet break.
A row reads "or" between two rules.

avoidWhen.when: Rows in a list need lines between them.
A card needs a boundary.
Form fields group under a title.

variants.useWhen: A rule between items of a row, as in a top bar.

card.job: Keep one primary action in reach while the page scrolls.
card.purpose: A 48px round accent button with a soft shadow that floats at a screen corner: a support chat, scroll to bottom. It grows slightly on hover and shrinks on press. Position it with your own layout; it has no label, so give it aria-label.
useWhen: One action is useful on every part of a long screen, such as opening support.
A phone screen has one main create action that must stay visible.

avoidWhen.when: The action belongs in a toolbar or a footer.
The launcher opens a chat window.
There are several actions.
An action is part of a form.

states.name: disabled
states.how: disabled

parts.role: The round button; holds one icon.

keyboard.does: Activates the button.

card.job: Give a control a label, a hint and room for one error.
card.purpose: The wrapper around one control: a label row, the control, a hint and an error slot. The hint gives way to the error when it appears, so a field never grows two lines of small print. Mark required fields with data-required on the label, not a red star. Errors are announced because the control points at them with aria-describedby.
useWhen: Any input, textarea, select or custom control that needs a visible label.
A control needs help text, a character counter or an error message under it.
An API parameter form is generated from a schema (data-variant="schema").

avoidWhen.when: Several fields make one titled group in a long create or edit form.
A setting is a label and a control on one row.
A switch or checkbox carries its own label text.

states.name: required
states.how: data-required on .fd-field-label

states.name: invalid
states.how: aria-invalid="true" on the control, text in .fd-field-error, aria-describedby pointing at it

states.name: over limit
states.how: data-state="limit" on the counter; "near" as it approaches maxlength

variants.useWhen: A label that is a mono parameter name with a quiet type, generated from an API schema.

parts.role: Row holding the label, the optional tag and the info button.
The required marker beside a label.
The (i) button beside the label; takes data-fd-tooltip.
Help text under the control; gives way to the error.
The single error message; hidden until needed.
Row under the control for hint and counter.
Live character count for a control with maxlength.

card.job: Add files by dropping them or browsing.
card.purpose: A dashed, sunken area that is also a button: click or press Enter to browse, or drop files. Dragging over it turns the line accent. Accepted files appear as rows in fd-filelist with progress, status and size. fd:files is cancelable so your app can run the upload and report progress with setFileProgress(); data-max-mb and accept reject files that do not fit.
useWhen: People attach one or several files, such as a sitemap, a CSV or a document.
Upload progress and per-file errors should show as rows.

avoidWhen.when: One small file is chosen as part of a plain form and no progress is needed.
The upload is an image avatar.
Files are only listed, not added.

states.name: dragover
states.how: data-state="dragover" while files are dragged over it

states.name: uploading
states.how: data-state="uploading" on a file row

states.name: error
states.how: data-state="error" on a file row, with a reason in .fd-file-status

states.name: done
states.how: data-state="done" on a file row

variants.useWhen: A compact one-line dropzone in a form row.

parts.role: The drop area; a label around the file input.
The icon that lifts on drag.
Progress, ready or the reason it failed.

card.job: Lay out fields and actions in a form that stays readable.
card.purpose: The form container: it stops at a readable width on its own (data-size sm, lg or full) and holds rows, columns and an actions bar. fd-form-row puts a label and what it does on the left and the control on the right; fd-form-cols fills the body in columns. Actions align right with the primary last; a destructive action sits alone at the left. data-fd-dirty shows a sticky unsaved-changes bar.
useWhen: A settings or create page holds several fields with a Save action.
Changes should trigger an unsaved-changes bar (data-fd-dirty, data-variant="sticky").

avoidWhen.when: A long form has titled groups that people scan.
One setting is a label and a control on a row of a list.
A short form belongs in a modal.
The form is a chat message.

states.name: dirty
states.how: data-dirty on a form with data-fd-dirty; shows the sticky actions

states.name: validated
states.how: data-fd-validate on the form; fd:invalid and fd:valid fire

variants.useWhen: A narrow form such as an invite or a sign-in.
A form with a wider measure.
A form made of sections that set their own width.
A row whose control aligns to the top of its text, as for a tall control.
On the actions bar: a destructive action at one end and the primary at the other.
Rows stack their control under the text at every width.
The actions float as an unsaved-changes bar.
A row keeps its label and a small control (a switch) side by side on phones.

Columns of fields that fill the body.
Text shown beside the actions, such as "Unsaved changes".

keyboard.does: Submits the form from a text input.

card.job: Group the fields of a long form under a title.
card.purpose: One titled group in a long create or edit form: a narrow head with a title and one line on the left (it stays in view while the body scrolls) and the fields on a white surface beside it. Below about 720px of form width the head stacks above the body. Use it inside a form with data-size="full".
useWhen: A create or edit form has more than one group: Basics, Callbacks, Access, Advanced.
People should scan titles and skip what they do not need.

avoidWhen.when: The form is short.
A card holds a single setting with a control.
The groups are steps in a flow.

variants.useWhen: The head stays above the body at every width.
A narrower body.
A wider body.

parts.role: The white surface holding the fields.

card.job: Lay out equal columns that fill the width and reflow.
card.purpose: An auto-filling grid. data-min sets the narrowest column (a size token from 4xs to 6xl, or full), data-cols the most columns, and data-span on a child covers several columns (or full). It drops columns on narrow screens by itself, so markup never sets a width.
useWhen: Cards, stats or fields sit in equal columns that should reflow on phones.
One child needs to span several columns (data-span).

avoidWhen.when: Children are in one line or one column.
Children are a list of cards that wrap with their own sizes.
avoidWhen.instead: The card grid class fd-card-grid in the content docs.

avoidWhen.when: A form has columns of fields.

card.job: Let one child take the space left over in a row.
card.purpose: A flex-grow helper: put it on the child of a row or stack that should absorb the remaining space, pushing its siblings to the ends. On an fd-divider it makes a rule that fills the row.
useWhen: A title should push its actions to the far end of a row.
A rule must fill the space on either side of an "or".

avoidWhen.when: Children should spread evenly.
Children are equal columns.
A band must fill the height of a centred screen.
avoidWhen.instead: The data-grow attribute on the shell band; see the shell docs.

parts.role: The class on the child that grows.

card.job: Draw a small symbol beside a label or on a button.
card.purpose: A 16px line icon from Fire's sprite, written as <i data-icon="name"> and drawn once at start (or as the fd-icon element with icon="name"). Sizes are 12, 14, 16, 20, 24 or 32 (plus sm and lg); tone sets its colour. It is decorative: name the control that holds it with a label. Change it with setIcon(el, name).
useWhen: A button, menu item or status needs a symbol to scan faster.
An empty state or a tile needs one glyph.

avoidWhen.when: The symbol is the only content and no label exists.
avoidWhen.instead: Add an aria-label or data-fd-tooltip to the control that holds it.

avoidWhen.when: A person's image is needed.
A brand mark is needed.
A tile with a coloured background holds the glyph.

states.name: filled
states.how: data-icon-fill on icons that have a filled form

variants.useWhen: Inside a dense chip or a badge.
Beside small text.
The default beside body text and in buttons.
A larger toolbar or a list row.
A prominent control or an empty state.
A tile or a header.
A hero or a large empty state.
The largest icon, as a lone symbol.
The small step of the icon scale.
The large step of the icon scale.
The icon marks the brand colour.
A quiet icon.
A positive state.
Something needs attention.
A destructive or failed state.
A neutral note.
An arrow that moves a little on hover, for an external link.

card.job: Mark a command, a path or a key inside a sentence.
card.purpose: Inline code in the mono face on a faint fill (fd-code), with a tone for status words, and a keyboard key cap (fd-kbd). Use it for identifiers, flags, file names and shortcuts that a person might copy or press, never for emphasis.
useWhen: A sentence names a file, a flag, an endpoint or a value.
A shortcut is shown as a key cap (fd-kbd), as in a search hint.

avoidWhen.when: The code is several lines or needs copying.
A command is shown to run.
The words are emphasis.
A status is shown.

variants.useWhen: A code span in the accent colour.
A quiet code span.
A passed value.
A value that needs a look.
A failed value.
An informational value.
A value still in progress.

card.job: Type one line of text, a URL, a key or a number.
card.purpose: The native input in Fire's field skin: a white surface, a 1px line drawn inside the box so nothing shifts between states, 36px tall. Hover darkens the line, focus swaps it for the accent and adds a halo, aria-invalid turns it danger. It also works as a span in the same shape to show a value people read but do not edit.

A read-only value must line up with real inputs (a span with the same class).

The value is a long answer over several lines.
The value is one of a fixed set.

A prefix, unit or button sits inside the field.
The value is a list of URLs, domains or emails.

states.how: disabled

A unit in mono after a number: ms, MB, requests.

A chevron that opens a list; used by the combobox.

A larger field.

The message when no option matches.

card.job: Enter a number and nudge it up or down.
card.purpose: A number input with steppers inside the field. Hold a stepper to repeat; steppers disable at min and max. Arrow keys and typing still work. fd:change fires with the new value.

elements.description:
A Fire chart drawn from data given as a property: line, area, bar and stacked charts, sparklines, donuts and
progress rings, heat grids and strips. The element is the chart's root: it carries the root class of its type
(`fd-chart`, `fd-sparkline`, `fd-donut` or `fd-heatgrid`) and the markup form's data-* attributes, holds the data
as the markup form's `<script type="application/json">`, and Fire's charts module draws the chart inside it, so it
looks and behaves exactly like the markup form. Setting `data` (or any attribute) redraws it, without the entrance
animation. Changing `type` to another kind of chart (say from `line` to `donut`) is not supported: render a new
element (in React or Vue, give it a new `key`).

Attributes mirror the markup form's `data-*` attributes; each applies to the types named. A function in the data
(a custom `yFormat`) is kept for cartesian charts, which are drawn from the object itself; the other types are
drawn from the JSON, so their formats are names.

attributes.name: area
attributes.description: Sparkline: fill the area under the line.

attributes.name: data
attributes.description: The chart's data: a `ChartConfig` for the cartesian types, an array of numbers for a sparkline, a `DonutConfig`, a `HeatgridConfig` or (strip) a `StripConfig`. As an attribute, JSON.

attributes.name: dot
attributes.description: Sparkline: mark the last point.

attributes.name: fluid

elements.description:
A Fire code block that highlights the text it is given. The element is the block's root: it carries
`class="fd-codeblock"` and the markup form's data-* attributes, renders the block's internals (an optional header
or copy button, then `<pre class="fd-codeblock-body"><code data-lang="…">`), puts `code` in it as text and lets
Fire's code module tokenise it into lines, so it looks and behaves exactly like the markup form. Unlike the markup
form inside a framework, Fire never rewrites text nodes the framework owns: changing `code` (or any attribute)
renders the internals afresh.

Languages: `json`, `bash`, `javascript`, `typescript`, `python` and their aliases (`sh`, `curl`, `js`, `ts`, `py`, …);
any other name shows plain text.

attributes.name: code
attributes.description: The code, as text (never HTML). As an attribute, the text itself.

attributes.name: collapse
attributes.description: Collapse to this height in px with a "Show all N lines" button when the code is taller (`data-collapse`).

attributes.name: copy
attributes.description: Add a copy button: in the header when there is a file name, otherwise floating in the corner.

attributes.name: filename
attributes.description: A file name shown in a header above the code (`.fd-codeblock-file`).

attributes.name: highlight
attributes.description: Lines to highlight, `3,5-7` (`data-highlight`).

attributes.name: language
attributes.description: Language for highlighting (the markup form's `data-lang` on `<code>`; `lang` is HTML's own attribute).

attributes.name: lines
attributes.description: Show line numbers (`data-lines`).

attributes.name: wrap
attributes.description: Soft-wrap long lines (`data-wrap`).

elements.description:
One of Fire's icons (a Lucide subset). The element is the icon's root, as `svg.fd-icon` is for the markup form:
it carries `class="fd-icon"`, `data-icon`, `data-size` and `aria-hidden="true"`, so every `.fd-icon` rule applies
to it, direct-child rules such as `.fd-btn > .fd-icon` included. Inside it, an SVG drawn from Fire's sprite fills
it (fire/base.css). Use it in framework code, where an `<i data-icon>` that replaces itself would break the
framework's reconciliation. The icon is decorative: name the control that holds it.

An unknown name draws nothing and logs a warning, as the markup form does.

attributes.name: icon
attributes.description: Icon name from Fire's set, for example `search` (the markup form's `data-icon`).

attributes.name: size
attributes.description: Size in px: 12, 14, 16 (the default), 20, 24 or 32 (the markup form's `data-size`).

properties.name: icon
properties.description: Icon name from Fire's set, for example `search` (the markup form's `data-icon`).

properties.description: Size in px: 12, 14, 16 (the default), 20, 24 or 32 (the markup form's `data-size`).

elements.description:
A Fire generative character field: terrain, waves, orbit, rain, grid, flame, halftone or spark. The element is
the field's root: it carries the markup form's `class="fd-ascii"`, `data-fd-ascii="…"`,
the other `data-*` attributes and `aria-hidden="true"`, and Fire's texture module draws its canvas inside it and owns
its size, colour and animation (12 fps on a shared frame loop, paused off screen, one still frame under reduced
motion). Being the field keeps Fire's layering rule, which puts a field between its container's background and its
content, working as it does for the markup form. Changing a property re-reads the settings and redraws.

The field fills its nearest positioned ancestor, or flows at the field height with `inline`. It is decorative.

attributes.name: animated
attributes.description: `true` or `false`; waves, orbit, rain and flame animate by default (`data-animate`; `animate` is a DOM method).

attributes.name: cell
attributes.description: Cell size in px, `7x12` (default) or `8` for square (`data-cell`).

attributes.name: fade
attributes.description: Fade out toward an edge: `left`, `right`, `top`, `bottom`, `x`, `y` or `radial` (`data-fade`).

attributes.name: inline
attributes.description: Flow in the page at the field height instead of filling the positioned ancestor (`data-inline`).

attributes.name: intensity
attributes.description: Luminance multiplier, default 1 (`data-intensity`).

attributes.name: interactive
attributes.description: Characters near the pointer step up the ramp (`data-interactive`).

attributes.name: marks
attributes.description: Draw `chars` (default) or `dots`, halftone discs (`data-style`).

attributes.name: origin
attributes.description: `x,y` in 0..1, the centre for orbit, flame, halftone and spark (`data-origin`).

attributes.name: pattern
attributes.description: The field: `terrain` (default), `waves`, `orbit`, `rain`, `grid`, `flame`, `halftone`, `spark` or a registered name (`data-fd-ascii`).

attributes.name: ramp
attributes.description: Character ramp: `default`, `soft`, `dense`, `glyph`, `rain`, or a literal ramp such as ` .:-=+*#` (`data-ramp`).

attributes.name: seed
attributes.description: Seed, a number or a string; defaults to the pattern name, so a page always looks the same (`data-seed`).

attributes.name: shape
attributes.description: `blob` clips the field to a soft, noisy disc (`data-shape`).

attributes.name: side
attributes.description: Terrain: the side that rises, `right` (default) or `left` (`data-side`).

attributes.name: speed
attributes.description: Time multiplier, default 1 (`data-speed`).

attributes.name: tone
attributes.description: Ink: `neutral` (default), `accent`, `contrast` or `strong` (`data-tone`).

attributes.name: variant
attributes.description: Grid: `flat` (default) or `perspective` (`data-variant`).
